clue.text: Any number hugged by show girl in seaside area

indicators.note: being hugged means held inside, so the number sits within the girl's name

parts.note: Maria is the heroine of the musicals West Side Story and The Sound of Music
N stands for an unspecified number in algebra

explanation.surface: A showgirl clutching a number appears somewhere by the seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: A marina is a harbour area for yachts, a typical development along a coastline.

clue.text: Make a new assessment of what someone says?

definitions.meaning: to mark again, as a teacher reassessing a test paper
a comment or observation spoken aloud

explanation.surface: A teacher wonders whether to re-grade a comment someone made.
explanation.definitionFit: Split as RE-MARK it means grade again; whole, it is a spoken comment, so both senses share one spelling.

clue.text: Bloomer is what wise men became aware of

definitions.meaning: a flowering plant, here a white-flowered bulb of the lily family

definitions.text: what wise men became aware of
definitions.meaning: the Magi noticed the bright star that led them to the infant Jesus

explanation.surface: A slip-up turns out to be something the wise men noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder or an item of underwear, but here it is literally something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a garden flower and the star the Magi followed in the nativity story.

clue.text: Soldier in a mess? No

definitions.meaning: a soldier who attends an officer or works in a military hospital
the opposite of messy, so neat and tidy

explanation.surface: Asks whether a soldier is eating in the mess, and answers no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mess' suggests the soldiers' dining hall, but the second reading is simply untidiness denied.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a military attendant and an adjective for being tidy and well arranged.

clue.text: During this action one may have a change of heart

definitions.text: During this action one may have a change of heart

parts.words: During this action one may have a change of heart
parts.note: a change of heart usually means changing one's mind, but here a literal heart is replaced in surgery

explanation.surface: Describes some event that makes a person change their mind.
explanation.definitionFit: In this surgical operation a patient may receive a donor heart, literally a new heart.

clue.text: Extra money in box about to be hidden

indicators.note: something hidden is tucked away within another piece, so the short word goes inside the container

parts.note: a case is a box or container
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Extra cash is stashed in a box to keep it out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extra money' is the definition, not part of the box's contents; 'to be hidden' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pay rise or uplift in funds is extra money, as when salaries go up.

clue.text: Herald rushed, went down for funny-sounding Oxford don

indicators.note: William Spooner was an Oxford don famous for swapping the starts of words, so his comical speech signals that swap

parts.note: tore means rushed, as in tore down the road
fell means went down or dropped

explanation.surface: A messenger hurried and tumbled over, all on behalf of a comical Oxford academic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for funny-sounding Oxford don' swaps the opening letters of TORE and FELL, giving FORE and TELL.
explanation.definitionFit: To herald something is to announce or predict its coming, i.e. to prophesy it.

clue.text: One expressing sorrow afterwards with soldiers getting buried

indicators.note: being buried means placed inside, so the soldiers go inside the word for afterwards

parts.note: later means afterwards
men is a common term for soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: A mourner grieves after soldiers are buried, like a war funeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who laments mourns or voices grief, so a mourner expressing sorrow.

clue.text: Rushed party with madame initially unmethodical

parts.note: ran means rushed
a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the word madame

explanation.surface: Someone dashed to a party with a lady in a haphazard way.
explanation.definitionFit: Random means haphazard, without any system or method.

clue.text: Enjoy what archaeologists do

definitions.meaning: slang for to like or appreciate, as in I really like that music

explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for liking something and also the plain verb for excavating ground.

clue.text: Princess good in Indian garment? Take a different view

parts.note: Di is the familiar name of Diana, Princess of Wales

indicators.note: in places the letter for good inside the garment

parts.note: a saree, also spelt sari, is a draped garment worn in India

explanation.surface: A princess looks fine in an Indian sari, though others think otherwise.
explanation.definitionFit: To differ in opinion is to hold another view from someone.

clue.text: Chaps needing to take off remain troubled

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed or upset, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Men eager to leave stay behind, worried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' looks like leaving or undressing, but the chaps are pilots needing to get airborne.
explanation.definitionFit: Aviators are men whose job requires getting aircraft off the ground.

clue.text: Local jerk's a daft drunk — will he do any job?

indicators.note: drunk means intoxicated and muddled, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Asks whether a silly, drunken local idiot will take on any work going.
explanation.definitionFit: A handyman versatile enough to turn a hand to every kind of work fits the phrase.

clue.text: Line given audibly?

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the word is the one that sounds like the line spoken

parts.note: a queue is a line of people waiting

explanation.surface: Asks whether a line of dialogue is being said out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: A queue (a line of people waiting, as in the US 'line') sounds the same as the actor's prompt. The whole clue also describes a prompt line spoken to an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre this is the spoken line or signal that tells an actor to come in.

clue.text: New student and father somewhere in Surrey

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
Esher is a town in Surrey, a county south-west of London

explanation.surface: A new student and their dad live in a place in Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: A British term for a first-year university student, a freshman.

clue.text: Sitting like a bird, right over egg — smart!

parts.note: O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
an egg is round like the letter O
to smart and to sting both mean to feel sharp pain

explanation.surface: Someone praises a bird sitting right over its egg as smart.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds perch or settle for the night on a roost, so sitting like one.

clue.text: Captains bring fish aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard means on a ship, so the fish goes inside the ship's letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a kipper is a smoked herring

explanation.surface: Ships' captains bring a catch of fish on board.
explanation.definitionFit: Those in command of boats are their masters, so a synonym for captains.

clue.text: Animal, look, chewing length of cloth

indicators.note: chewing means having in the mouth, so the measure goes inside the word for look

parts.note: to gaze is to look steadily
an ell is an old measure of cloth, about 45 inches

explanation.surface: An animal stares while chewing a strip of fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazelle is a type of slender antelope, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Floral decoration that is left upside down

indicators.note: in a down clue, upside down means the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, meaning that is

explanation.surface: A floral decoration has been left hanging upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hawaiian garland of flowers worn around the neck.

clue.text: Lady succeeded ultimately, having superior game

indicators.note: ultimately picks out the final letter of the word succeeded

parts.note: U means upper class, the socially superior in British usage
chess is a board game

explanation.surface: A lady finally wins because she plays a better game.
explanation.definitionFit: A duchess is a noblewoman, the wife of a duke, so a titled lady.

clue.text: Convey obvious message or depart in silence?

definitions.meaning: to be so evident that nobody needs to state it
to leave without speaking, read literally

explanation.surface: Either send a clear signal or slip away quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means be self-evident; read literally it means leave without a word.

clue.text: Small farmer in the old Arab territory

parts.note: ye is an old form of the
Oman is an Arab country on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A smallholder lives in an old Arab land.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a yeoman was a man holding and farming a small estate of his own.

clue.text: Relations terribly insecure, having abandoned biblical city

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the remaining letters are jumbled
abandoned means left behind, so the city's letters drop out of the word insecure

parts.note: Ur of the Chaldees was Abraham's city in the Bible

explanation.surface: Insecure relatives have fled an ancient city mentioned in the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having abandoned' takes UR out of INSECURE, leaving INSECE, and 'terribly' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nieces are family members, daughters of one's siblings, so relations.

clue.text: Walked endlessly in plain territory

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: stepped means walked

explanation.surface: Someone walked on and on through flat country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' looks like an adjective meaning simple; it is the noun for flat grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: A steppe is a vast treeless grassland in Eurasia, so territory that is a plain.

clue.text: Blessed and married after salutation

indicators.note: after means the word for married comes behind the greeting

parts.note: hallo is a greeting, a variant of hello
wed means married

explanation.surface: A couple were blessed and married after a greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallowed means made holy or sanctified, so blessed.

clue.text: Tool with chrome, odd bits flaking off

indicators.note: the first, third and fifth letters peel away, leaving the even-placed ones

explanation.surface: A chrome tool is shedding bits of its plating.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoe is a long-handled garden implement for weeding, an example of a tool.

clue.text: Course taken by some in parliament re-elected

indicators.note: some in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Describes a course of action taken by some re-elected MPs.
explanation.definitionFit: An entree is a dish served at a meal, a course before or as the main.

clue.text: Warbled with a lurch, not finishing drink

parts.note: sang means warbled

indicators.note: not finishing means the word stops short of its final letter

parts.note: to reel is to stagger or lurch

explanation.surface: Someone sang, staggering, without finishing their drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangaree is a spiced drink of wine or spirits, a relative of sangria.
